picked.t: 베트남, 5,300억 원 규모 ‘북남고속철 설계' 韓3개사 컨소시엄과 계약 체결
picked.body: 지난 21일 열린 베트남 북남고속철도 설계 계약 체결식 당시 모습. (사진=베트남 건설부) 베트남의 국토대동맥이 될 북남고속철도 건설사업이 본격적으로 추진된다. 북남고속철도 발주처인 베트남 건설부 탕롱(Thang Long) 사업관리위원회는 타당성조사(F/S)와 기본설계(FEED)를 맡을 컨소시엄과 컨설팅 계약을 체결하며, 본 사업 이전 사전 준비 착수를 공식화했다. 탕롱사업관리위원회는 지난 25일 한국과 프랑스, 베트남 등 8개 회사로 구성된 글로벌 컨소시엄과 10조2,430억 동(3억9,620만여 달러, 5,320억 원 상당) 규모의 북남고속철도 컨설팅 계약을 체결했다. 이날 서명식에서 부이 쑤언 융(Bui Xuan Dung) 건설부 차관은 “이번 사업은 베트남 최초로 진행되는 대규모 고속철도 사업으로, 복잡한 기술과 전문 지식을 필요로 한다. 이런 점에서 타당성조사와 기본설계는 사업의 실현가능성과 품질, 투자 효율성을 결정하는 데 핵심적인 부분”이라고 강조했다. 융 차관은 이번 서명식을 실질적 사업 추진 단계로 넘어가는 이정표라고 평가하며 주요 4대 과제를 컨소시엄과 탕롱사업관리위원회에 주문했다. 여기에는 △핵심 인력 신속 동원 및 전문 관리 체계 구축, 각 사업 부문에 대한 진척도 관리 계획, 정확하고 신뢰할 수 있는 조사 자료 확보  △타당성조사 보고서 및 기본설계, 베트남 실정에 부합하고 장기적 운영 및 유지보수 측면에서 안전성과 효율성을 보장할 수 있는 최첨단 기술 선정△진척도 및 품질관리 등 계약 이행 결과 전반에 대한 탕롱사업관리위원회의 책임 △사업 진행 상황과 품질 관리에 있어 엄격한 규율 적용 등이 포함된다. 융 차관은 “컨소시엄은 국내 전문가의 역할을 효과적으로 활용해 기술과 관리 경험 공유에 집중함으로써, 베트남 기술자들이 단계적으로 기술을 습득할 수 있도록 힘써야 한다”며 “TV02 패키지의 성공 기준은 품질 높은 타당성조사 보고서와 동기화된 기본설계, 표준적인 입찰 서류 체계로, 각 진행 상황은 주요 이정표가 수립되어야 하며, 이를 통해 다음 단계 진행을 위한 토대를 마련해야 한다”고 강조했다. 탕롱사업관리위원회의 딘 꽁 민(Dinh Cong Minh) 위원장 또한 계약 체결 직후 “컨소시엄이 인력과 전문가를 충분히 투입하고 세부 추진 계획을 세워 국제적인 역량과 경험으로 사업의 품질과 일정을 보장해달라”고 요청했다. KTX 열차. (사진=코레일) 프랑스 시스트라(SYSTRA)의 패트릭 데스포르주(Patrick Desforges)는 컨소시엄을 대표해 탕롱사업위원회와 건설부, 관계 기관, 노선이 지나는 지방과 긴밀히 협력하겠다고 약속했다. 노선이 길고 기술 요건이 복잡한 만큼 현실에 맞는 계획을 세우고, 비용을 엄밀하게 따지고, 여러 대안을 꼼꼼히 검토해 당국이 결정을 내릴 근거를 제공하겠다는 설명이다. 컨소시엄이 체결한 계약은 기본조사와 타당성조사, 기본설계, 입찰 서류 작성 등을 담은 TV02 패키지 용역으로, 앞서 발주처인 탕롱사업관리위원회는 22일 컨소시엄 선정 결과를 승인·발표한 바 있다. 프랑스 철도 엔지니어링 업체 시스트라가 이끌고 국가철도공단, 삼보, 유신 등 한국 3개사와 베트남 4개사가 참여한 글로벌 컨소시엄은 향후 30개월간 본 공사에 앞서 사업의 큰 틀을 그리는 설계 작업에 임하게 된다. 탕롱사업관리위원회는 이를 바탕으로 2028년 말 본 사업을 착공한다는 계획이다. 베트남 북남고속철도 노선도. (이미지=국토교통부) 앞서 베트남 국회가 승인한 계획에 따르면, 북남고속철도는 15개 성·시를 거쳐 하노이와 호치민시를 잇는 총연장 1,541km 노선으로, 총사업비 1,713조5,480억 동(665억 달러)이 투입되는 베트남 역사상 최대 규모의 철도 인프라 사업이다. 본 노선은 설계 속도 시속 350km의 표준궤(1,435mm) 복선철도로 계획됐으며, 전체 구간에는 여객역 23개와 화물역 5개가 들어선다. 북남고속철도는 완공 시, 하노이와 호치민시 간 이동시간이 5시간대로 단축, 국토 전역이 일일 생활권으로 묶이게 돼 베트남 경제 성장을 가속화할 핵심 동력이 될 것으로 기대를 모으고 있다.

picked.t: Japan looks to Bangladesh, Nepal for farmhands as Vietnamese recruiters struggle to fill jobs
picked.body: Tokyo-based Mirai, which trains and places skilled foreign workers, has introduced its first Bangladeshi candidates for farm work, Kyodo News reported. Two students from one of its partner schools in Bangladesh passed Japan's specified skilled worker agriculture exam in August and received job offers from an agricultural company in northeastern Aomori Prefecture, where they are due to head in the coming months. "I am very excited to go to Japan and learn about Japanese agriculture," Ahasan Habib, 21, from Mymensingh in northern Bangladesh, told the Japanese news site. "I want to make good use of my experience and take proper care of chickens." The other candidate, Siam Ur Rahman, 20, from Barisal in southern Bangladesh, said he wanted "to work very hard" in Japan and was looking forward to touching snow. The two will join Japan's Type 1 specified skilled workers in agriculture, whose stays are generally capped at five years. Their number rose 26% from a year earlier to 44,050 at the end of June, according to the Immigration Services Agency. Indonesia remained the largest supplier with 18,255 farm workers, up 45%, followed by Vietnam with 10,261, up 11%. Vietnam's share of the sector fell from about 26% a year earlier to 23%, although it is still the largest source of Type 1 workers across all fields, with 163,154 of the 425,961 in Japan. South Asian farm workers numbers remain small but are climbing fast. Bangladesh's count jumped 127% to 334, Sri Lanka's climbed 60% to 638 and Nepal's rose 30% to 916. Yuji Nomura, general manager of the career advisory division at Mirai's parent company Sustainable Holdings, told Kyodo News that rising wages in Vietnam, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries were making it harder for Japan to attract farm workers from there. "We're seeing a shift to South Asia for labor supply sources," he said. To qualify for specified skilled worker status in agriculture, candidates should pass the N4 beginner-level Japanese test as well as written and practical farming exams, Nomura said. Sustainable Holdings runs Mirai partner schools in the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and has added schools in Sri Lanka and Nepal. Japan's farms face chronic labor shortages due to aging and other factors. Including technical intern trainees, 67,905 foreigners held specified skilled worker or trainee status in agriculture at the end of 2025, according to government data. Noriyuki Takakura, a director at Sustainable Holdings, said workers from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal were highly regarded for their seriousness and diligence. The company offers free tuition at Mirai partner schools across Asia and helps students find housing in Japan. "We will gradually expand agricultural classes in each country," Takakura said. In Vietnam, Japan was the top destination for workers going abroad in 2025, receiving more than 64,600, but it has slipped to second place this year. Of the 114,276 Vietnamese who left to work overseas on contracts in the first 10 months, 50,473 went to Taiwan and 45,658 to Japan, according to the Department of Overseas Labor Management. Pham Van Trong, human resources manager at a Hanoi company that has sent workers to Japan for more than a decade, including in agriculture, told VnExpress that each job order once drew seven or eight applicants but now gets about two per position. The company's supply of candidates has fallen about 60%, he said. Trong said more jobs at home were part of the reason, with unskilled construction work now paying around VND20 million ($770). But he blamed mainly the weaker yen, which once fetched VND200-220 and now fetches about VND160-170. Workers' total incomes are 1.2 to 1.5 times what they were a decade ago, but their savings have not kept pace. On VND30-40 million ($1,150-1,540) a month, they used to send home VND20-25 million ($770-960), and they still send about the same. "With the yen sliding and savings not growing, workers will think twice," Trong said.

picked.t: Inside Binh Tay, the 96-year-old Chinatown market in HCMC
picked.body: Binh Tay Market is situated between Thap Muoi, Le Tan Ke, Phan Van Khoe, and Tran Binh streets in Binh Tay Ward, an area with a large Hoa community, people of Chinese ancestry. Besides serving locals, the market is a regular stop for tourists visiting HCMC. According to Nguyen Thi Ngoc Chau, deputy director of the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market was built in 1930. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. The market, which was renovated in 2016, retains its original architecture. It spreads over 25,000 square meters with a floor area of more than 17,000 square meters, and has one main gate and 12 side entrances. It has a tall tower with four clock faces. The yin-yang tiled roofs are arranged in overlapping layers and curve upward at the corners. In 2017, the market was recognized as a city architectural and artistic heritage site. In 2022, it was named a tourist attraction of HCMC. According to Le Hong Minh, head of the business management team at the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market has 2,358 stalls that sell more than 30 product categories. Its main goods include spices, groceries, clothing, and confectionery. Data from 2023 to 2026 shows that 73% of visitors to the market are international. It receives 120,000 foreign visitors a year, most of them brought on guided tours. On Sept. 8, a group of 10 Indian tourists led by Rohan and his wife spent over an hour exploring the market and buying more than a dozen handmade bags as gifts. Rohan praised its architecture and range of goods but said the products were similar to those at other markets in town. Stalls selling dry goods and spices are located near the market's main gate. Minh said shopping preferences at Binh Tay vary by region. European and American tourists buy handicrafts and clothing. Southeast Asian visitors shop for confectionery, tea, coffee, and bamboo goods. Northeast Asian tourists prefer specialties, dried foods, and herbal medicines. Besides shopping, the market has a food area serving dishes from all over Vietnam. Binh Tay Market plans to combine shopping with cultural and culinary experiences by offering heritage tours, spiritual visits, performances recreating old Chinatown, craft workshops with artisans, and Chinese-Vietnamese cuisine. picked.t: Vietnamese woman wins over Brazilian parents-in-law with traditional dishes made from local ingredients
picked.body: In late October, while visiting a park in the state of Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, she cut a few wild banana leaves to bring home and wrap banh tet (Vietnamese sticky rice cake), one of her husband’s favorite Vietnamese dishes. To help him and his parents like Vietnamese food, the 36-year-old from southern Dong Nai province had earlier spent two years overcoming numerous challenges and ingredient shortages. She had met her husband, a doctor, when he came to HCMC on a vacation. They dated and got married in 2019, after which she moved to Rio de Janeiro with him. At first, she struggled to adapt to the local cuisine. Brazilian meals primarily consist of loose, long-grain rice served with black beans stewed and salted meat, and consist of very few brothy soups. Thuy craved Vietnamese noodles and pickled vegetables, but it was very difficult to find Vietnamese ingredients. There were only two stores in Rio de Janeiro selling Asian ingredients such as fish sauce, tofu, fermented tofu, and rice paper, and the store closest to her house was a 45-minute drive away. By late 2020, when she was pregnant with her first child, Natalia, her craving for Vietnamese dishes had grown even stronger, and she began thinking about how to cook some of them using locally available ingredients. She thinly sliced cucumbers and carrots, and tossed them with salt, garlic, and chili to make quick pickles. She also bought mung beans and sprouted them to get fresh bean sprouts. Noticing that locals ate a lot of fish and local markets sold okra, pineapple, and tomatoes, she used these ingredients to make canh chua ca (Vietnamese sour fish soup). Her parents-in-law were surprised the first time they saw a bowl of fish and vegetable soup, as Brazilians are used to eating grilled fish or pan-seared fillets. However, after taking a spoonful of the broth, they were amazed at how the mild sourness from the pineapple and tomatoes completely eliminated any fishy odor. "After my daughter was born, I wanted her and the whole family to get to know and love Vietnamese food," Thuy says. With that goal in mind, she decided to transform her in-laws' palates. Thuy's husband has been a vegetarian for many years, but vegetarian diets in Brazil can be quite monotonous as local food usually features fatty meats. Even traditional stewed black beans are typically simmered with salted meat, leaving vegetarians with few choices beyond plain white rice, boiled cassava, or lettuce salads. Thuy bought tofu, mushrooms, rice vermicelli, and rice paper from the Asian stores, and combined them with tomatoes and carrots from local markets to create vegetarian dishes. She made fried tofu in tomato sauce, mushrooms braised in pepper sauce, stir-fried rice vermicelli with vegetables, and vegetarian summer rolls served with peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. While hiking in the mountains, she noticed clumps of wild bamboo shoots, which locals do not eat since they regard them as just another forest plant. Thuy dug up the shoots, peeled them, boiled them multiple times to remove the bitterness, and stir-fried them with garlic or cooked them in soup. When Thuy’s husband saw her bring home wild bamboo shoots from the forest and season them with garlic and chili, he hesitated at first. However, after trying a bite of the stir-fry, he was surprised by its crisp texture and delicate sweetness. He finished the entire plate in one sitting and immediately fell in love with the dish. In Brazil, jackfruits grow abundantly along roadsides and in parks, but locals don’t eat them and simply let ripe jackfruits fall to the ground. Thuy once picked an unripe jackfruit, trimmed off the peel full of sap, boiled it until tender, and used half to make shredded jackfruit salad and braised the other half in black pepper sauce. Because Vietnamese herbs were hard to find, she substituted peppermint for Vietnamese mint. Her husband took a bite and was amazed by the chewy, nutty texture of the shredded jackfruit that was infused with garlic and chili. "The dish feels light on the stomach and isn't heavy or greasy," he says. He asks his wife to cook Vietnamese food three times every week now. Thuy's parents-in-law live on their own and occasionally visit their son’s family. In the beginning, the difference in eating habits would lead to many awkward situations. Once, while she was braising pork ribs, the pungent smell of fish sauce filled the kitchen, and it alarmed her in-laws so much that they flung open the windows and took refuge in the living room. When she craved pickled mustard greens during her pregnancy, her husband drove nearly an hour to buy the greens for her to pickle. After seeing white foam forming in the jar and the greens changing color, her mother-in-law told her son to throw the pickles away. "I was heartbroken over the wasted batch, but I figured they were only worried because they cared about their daughter-in-law," Thuy says. 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남의 여권 파워가 세계 85위로 직전 발표 대비 4계단 도약했다. 영국 국제 시민권·영주권 자문회사 헨리앤파트너스(Henley & Partners)가 최근 발표한 '2026년 11월 헨리여권지수(Henley Passport Index)'에 따르면, 베트남의 여권 파워는 세계 85위로 10월 대비 4계단 상승했다. 베트남 여권 소지자는 전 세계 50개국에 무비자 또는 도착비자 형태로 입국이 가능해 코모로와 기니비사우, 요르단과 같은 순위를 나타냈다. 직전 조사와 비교하면 무비자로 입국할 수 있는 국가는 1개 늘었다. 베트남 여권 순위는 올 들어 지속적으로 오르내리는 모습을 보였다. 자세히 살펴보면, 1월 발표에서는 86위를 기록한 뒤, 3월 84위로 2계단 상승했다. 이어 6월 87위, 10월 89위로 약세를 보이더니 이번에 다시 반등했다. 동남아 중에서 베트남은 캄보디아(88위)와 라오스(90위), 미얀마(92위)에 앞섰다. 반면, 싱가포르(1위)와 말레이시아(6위), 브루나이(19위), 태국(64위), 인도네시아(67위), 필리핀(72위)에는 뒤처졌다. 한편, 싱가포르 여권 소지자는 전 세계 193개 목적지에 무비자로 입국할 수 있어 세계에서 가장 강력한 여권 지위를 유지했다. 다음으로는 일본과 아랍에미리트(UAE)가 188개국으로 2위를, 한국은 187개국으로 3위를 차지했다. 여권 순위 최하위 5개국에는 예멘(100위), 파키스탄, 이라크, 시리아, 아프가니스탄(104위)이 포함됐다. 이들 국가 여권 소지자의 무비자 입국 가능국가는 22~30개국에 불과했다. 헨리여권지수는 국제항공운송협회(IATA)의 독점 자료를 바탕으로 전 세계 227개 국가 및 지역의 이동 자유도를 추적, 글로벌 이동 자유도를 나타내는 핵심 지표로, 전체 199개국 여권을 대상으로 사전 비자 없이 입국 가능한 국가 수를 집계해 연중 정기적으로 발표된다.

picked.t: 8 tidal gates shield Ho Chi Minh City streets from flooding
picked.body: Tran Xuan Soan Street in former District 7 remained dry at 5:30 p.m., despite being a regular flooding hotspot whenever water levels in nearby rivers and canals rise. Just a month earlier, a stretch of more than 3 km of the road was submerged, with floodwaters reaching halfway up vehicle wheels and forcing many commuters to push their motorbikes through the water. The road's protection from flooding is attributed to the newly completed VND10 trillion (US$387 million) tidal control system. At noon on Wednesday, project investor Trung Nam Group lowered the sluice gates, closing all eight tidal control structures at the mouths of major rivers in the city's urban core. The system has helped reduce high-tide flooding in several areas in the city's south, including parts of the former districts 1, 7 and 8, and Nha Be District. The project is expected to mitigate flooding across 570 sq.km of the inner city, equivalent to one-fourth of the city’s land area before the merger, benefiting approximately 6.5 million people. The road's protection from flooding is attributed to the newly completed VND10 trillion (US$387 million) tidal control system. At noon on Wednesday, project investor Trung Nam Group lowered the sluice gates, closing all eight tidal control structures at the mouths of major rivers in the city's urban core. The system has helped reduce high-tide flooding in several areas in the city's south, including parts of the former districts 1, 7 and 8, and Nha Be District. The project is expected to mitigate flooding across 570 sq.km of the inner city, equivalent to one-fourth of the city’s land area before the merger, benefiting approximately 6.5 million people. The Tan Thuan tidal control gate is operational, helping keep areas around Tran Xuan Soan and Truong Dinh Hoi streets relatively dry. About 8 km away, Pham Huu Lau Street also remained free of the flooding that affected it last month. The busy road has frequently suffered severe traffic disruptions during previous floods. picked.t: Nutifood forms US nutrition science alliance with four partners
picked.body: Nutifood announced the establishment of Nutifood American Nutrition Science in Kansas on Nov. 24. The new entity will connect the company's research and product development capabilities with the U.S. nutrition science, dairy ingredients, and manufacturing sectors. The launch was marked by a signing ceremony with Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), witnessed by representatives of the Vietnamese Consulate General in San Francisco and senior U.S. dairy industry executives. Building on a scientific foundation The move builds on Nutifood's more than 25 years of research and development (R&D) experience across Vietnam, Sweden, and Australia, where it has developed nutrition solutions for different consumer needs. In early 2026, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted a patent for the company's proprietary FDI formula, expanding its intellectual property portfolio. The U.S. offers an opportunity for Nutifood to tap into an advanced dairy ecosystem spanning ingredients, manufacturing, research, and clinical science. Through its new entity, the company aims to combine its intellectual property and research expertise with U.S. scientific and industrial resources, moving beyond conventional exports to participate more deeply in the nutrition value chain. Four U.S. partners Nutifood is forming a Nutrition Science Alliance with the California Milk Advisory Board (CMAB), California Dairies, Inc. (CDI), DFA, and Natural Immune Systems Laboratories (NIS Labs). Each partner brings different capabilities: CMAB connects the company with California's dairy industry and products bearing the Real California Milk seal; CDI provides large-scale dairy processing and manufacturing; DFA contributes R&D and formula innovation; and NIS Labs offers laboratory testing, preclinical studies, and human research. By combining these capabilities across ingredients, manufacturing, R&D, and clinical research, Nutifood aims to improve control over product development and meet scientific and quality standards in international markets. "Every age group, body condition, and stage of life requires specialized nutrition solutions grounded in scientific evidence. That is why Nutifood American Nutrition Science is not simply looking for ingredient suppliers or manufacturing facilities in the United States," said Tran Bao Minh, vice chairman of Nutifood. "We are building strategic partnerships with CMAB, CDI, DFA, and NIS Labs to combine advanced technology and research capabilities in order to develop new nutrition standards for consumers worldwide." Through its U.S. entity and four strategic partnerships, Nutifood aims to strengthen its international competitiveness by combining its research capabilities and patented technologies with American scientific and manufacturing resources.

picked.t: “아침은 하노이, 점심은 호치민” 베트남, ‘남북고속철’ 2028년 착공 목표…사업비 670억 달러
picked.body: KTX 열차. (사진=코레일) 베트남이 국토대동맥이 될 북남고속철도의 착공 목표 시점을 2028년 말로 제시했다. 앞서 베트남 정부가 세운 착공 목표(2026년 말)보다는 2년 늦은 일정이다. 앞서 베트남 건설부 산하 탕롱(Thang Long) 사업관리위원회의 응우옌 쭝 선(Nguyen Trung Son) 부위원장은 “컨설팅 업체 선정 후 구체적인 일정이 확정됐다”며 “컨소시엄은 용역기간 30개월 내 4가지 주요 목표를 달성해야 하며, 이 계획대로라면 사업은 2028년 말 착공을 목표로 한다”고 25일 밝혔다. 탕롱사업관리위원회에 따르면, 컨소시엄은 3개월차까지 북남고속철도에 적용할 기술 표준과 기본 설계 요건을 제시해 이후 진행될 측량과 계산, 설계 작업의 토대를 마련할 예정이다. 이후 컨소시엄은 13개월차까지 △노선 경로 △주요 통제 지점 △기술 옵션들을 담은 중간 보고서를 제출해야 한다. 이러한 결정사항들은 타당성조사가 최종 확정되기 전, 프로젝트의 주요 기술적 솔루션을 구성하는 자료로 활용된다. 이어 27개월차에는 타당성조사 보고서를 심사위원회와 건설부에 제출해 검토를 받고, 30개월차까지 관계 기관의 최종 승인을 받을 것으로 예상된다. 컨소시엄은 타당성조사와 함께 내년 1분기부터 3분기까지 발주처의 지시 아래 관련 기관과 함께 노선을 따라 지형·지질 조사를 수행하게 된다. 또한 2027년부터 진행될 토지보상·재정착 등 작업이 원활히 이뤄질 수 있도록 부지정리 경계를 각 지방당국에 조기 인계할 계획이다. 베트남 북남고속철도 노선도. (이미지=국토교통부) 앞서 탕롱사업관리위원회는 북남고속철도의 타당성조사(F/S)·기본설계(FEED)를 포함한 ‘TV02 패키지’ 용역의 사업자 선정 결과를 지난 22일 승인·발표한 바 있다. 최종 낙찰가는 10조2,430억 동(3억9,750만여 달러)으로 발주처가 제시한 10조7,820억 동(4억1,840만여 달러)보다 5,390억 동(2,090만여 달러) 적었다. 컨설팅 용역을 수주한 컨소시엄은 한국과 프랑스, 베트남 등 3개국 기업으로 구성된 글로벌 컨소시엄으로, 참여 기업을 살펴보면, 프랑스 철도 엔지니어링 업체 시스트라(SYSTRA)가 주도하며, 한국 기업으로는 국가철도공단, 삼보, 유신 등이 참여했다. 베트남에서는 교통운송설계자문총공사(TEDI), 남부교통운송설계자문회사(TEDI SOUTH), 교통운송투자건설자문회사(TRICC), 호앙롱건설자문회사 4곳이 이름을 올렸다. 선정 결과가 승인됨에 따라 탕롱사업관리위원회는 계약 체결을 위한 절차 진행을 낙찰된 컨소시엄에 요청한 상태다. 계약 서명식은 이달 말 열릴 예정이다. 북남고속철도는 하노이 응옥호이역과 호치민시 투티엠역을 잇는 총연장 1,541km 노선으로, 15개 성·시를 지난다. 설계 속도 시속 350km, 축중(차축 1개당 하중) 22.5톤의 표준궤(1,435mm) 복선철도로 지어지며 여객역 23곳과 화물역 5곳이 들어선다. 예비 총사업비는 약 673억4,000만 달러로 베트남 역사상 최대 규모의 철도 인프라 사업이다. 완공되면 하노이와 호치민시 사이 이동 시간이 5시간대로 줄어 베트남 전역을 하나의 '일일 생활권'으로 묶어주는 국가 경제의 새로운 동력이 될 것으로 기대를 모은다. 베트남 정부 계획상 타당성조사 보고서는 2026~2028년 작성과 승인을 마치고, 본사업에 들어가 2035년까지 대부분을 마무리하는 것이 목표다.

picked.t: Vietnam has strong potential to attract billions in foreign capital: experts
picked.body: Experts shared these views at the HDBank Global Capital Conference 2026, themed "Global Capital – Vietnam's Aspirations," which brought together nearly 1,000 delegates in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi on Wednesday. Attendees included Philipp Rösler, vice chairman of HD Securities; Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, chairwoman of Sovico Group; Kim Byoungho, chairman of HDBank; and Darryl James Dong, former head of the International Finance Corporation's (IFC) office in Ho Chi Minh City, along with financial executives, experts and domestic and international investors. Golden opportunity to attract foreign capital Speaking at the conference, Rösler said Vietnam would need approximately $1.5 trillion in investment to achieve double-digit growth from 2026 to 2030, while the state budget could cover only about 20% of the total. This highlights the need to develop domestic capital markets and expand access to international funding. "Capital does not fear risk, but it always fears uncertainty," he said. Capital can move worldwide in search of growth, Rösler said, but stays only where rules are clear, information is transparent and commitments are honored. FTSE Russell's upgrade of Vietnam's stock market and the launch of the Vietnam International Financial Center are complementary milestones. To capitalize on them, he called for consistent and predictable policies, gradual market opening and compliance with international corporate governance standards. From a banking perspective, Kim Byoungho said Vietnam's integration into global financial markets should rest on three pillars: capital, standards and partnerships. HDBank, Sovico and their partners are expanding cooperation in London, New York, Tokyo, Singapore and Seoul to broaden fundraising opportunities and support Vietnamese companies' international expansion. Thomas Nguyen, a senior international stock market expert, said the upgrade would make Vietnam's stock market more accessible to foreign investors. However, attracting global capital remains challenging as much of investors' attention is currently focused on artificial intelligence and technology. He identified four potential drivers of Vietnam's stock market growth in 2027: increased foreign inflows following the upgrade, infrastructure reforms, possible shifts in global capital as the AI investment boom cools, and lower deposit interest rates. Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao said Vietnam's ability to implement programs and projects quickly was a key advantage. She cited the resolution of trading system congestion at the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange within 90 days using domestic technology, and an online platform that raised more than $400 million for the Covid-19 vaccine fund. She also stressed the importance of reliable local partners and regulatory support in investment decisions. Thao said investors who participated in Vietjet's initial public offering (IPO) have seen their investments increase more than fivefold, while those who bought HDBank shares in its 2018 IPO have gained approximately sixfold. She said both companies have maintained commitments to transparency, corporate governance and long-term value creation. Vietnam also has significant investment potential in infrastructure, technology, education, healthcare, culture and human development, she said. "I hope investors, particularly international investors, will seize the opportunities offered by Vietnam's capital market, build a better future for themselves, and grow alongside this market," she added. Gateways connecting Vietnam with global investment markets A highlight of the conference was a bell-ringing ceremony marking the IPO of HD Securities Joint Stock Company (HDS), which has a valuation of nearly $1.8 billion. Representatives of regulators, HDBank and HD Securities joined the ceremony at the HCMC and Hanoi venues. HD Securities Chairman Vu Huu Dien said the company aims to become one of Vietnam's three largest securities firms by 2030 and lead the market in smart trading platforms and AI-powered governance. It also plans to establish a securities subsidiary at the Vietnam International Financial Center. CEO Nguyen Ha Quynh said HD Securities is focusing on four business areas: investment banking, securities brokerage and margin lending, treasury operations, and investment and proprietary trading. The company aims to raise shareholders' equity to VND77-78 trillion ($3 million) by 2030 while maintaining a return on equity above 20%. Its IPO is expected to raise VND4.737 trillion ($183.38 million), with 60% allocated to margin lending, 30% to financial instrument investments and the remainder to other business activities. During a question-and-answer session, Tran Hoai Nam, standing deputy CEO of HDBank, said the bank aims to raise at least $2 billion annually from international sources. picked.t: South Korea's passport slips to third place, trailing Japan and UAE
picked.body: Previously, it shared second place with Japan and the UAE, both of which retain their positions in the latest ranking with visa-free access to 188 destinations. Singapore continues holding the world's most powerful passport, allowing visa-free entry to 193 destinations. The U.S. passport rose one spot to ninth in the index, with visa-free access increasing from 179 to 180 destinations. Vietnam's passport has climbed four places to 85th as its holders can enter 50 destinations worldwide without obtaining a visa in advance. The five weakest passports belong to Pakistan, Yemen, Iraq, Syria, and Afghanistan. The Henley Passport Index tracks global travel freedom across 227 countries and territories, using data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA). It ranks 199 passports based on the number of destinations their holders can enter without obtaining a visa in advance. Updated regularly throughout the year to reflect changes in visa policies, the index is widely regarded as a key measure of global mobility.
